ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, senior officers, authorised signatories, and — given the ISIC 5222 crew recruitment scope — placement managers against: (i) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the United States OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, with elevated emphasis because SWIFT wire and multi-currency payroll rails create a USD correspondent clearing nexus; (iii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list and UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions; (iv) South African domestic sanctions and notices published by the Financial Intelligence Centre and DIRCO under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Related and Organised Crime Act; and (v) FATF public statements and jurisdictional advisories. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified on a risk-sensitive basis under FICA section 28A, covering foreign and domestic PEPs, family members and close associates, triggering enhanced due diligence, source of funds/wealth verification, and senior management approval for any PEP or sanctions red flag.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Online Filing Portal — Companies and Intellectual Property Commission of South Africa (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressible in the Latin character script (English or Afrikaans) for electronic filing; a private company's name must conclude with '(Pty) Ltd'. Foreign-language words require Latin-script transliteration and, where necessary, an explanatory translation acceptable to CIPC. Names must satisfy the Companies Act 71 of 2008 section 11 and Companies Regulations 2011 Regulation 13, and must not be offensive, misleading, infringing of intellectual property, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name/trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Mutual Bank, Insurer/Assurer, Trust, Trustee, Unit Trust, Stock Exchange, or other financial sector terms (prior Prudential Authority and financial-sector regulator approval required)
Limited (restricted to public companies or entities holding express authorization)
South Africa, National, Government, Municipal, or words implying an official state connection (prior ministerial/state-sector authorization required)
University, College, or education-sector descriptors (registration with the relevant education authority required)
Building Society, Chamber of Mines, or other historically restricted statutory expressions
Offensive, obscene, or trademark-protected terms under Companies Act section 11 and Regulation 13
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC rejects a proposed name, the applicant should submit a written reconsideration application through the CIPC (Form CoR 9.6 / name reconsideration procedure) within the prescribed period, annexing a legal memorandum demonstrating compliance with section 11 of the Companies Act and Regulation 13 of the Companies Regulations, 2011. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may lodge an application with the Companies Tribunal under section 160 of the Companies Act to determine and direct registration of the disputed name, with a final alternative reserved via South African High Court review. Concurrently, the agent should re-file a fresh name reservation with secondary variants to preserve the timeline. The initial 180-day reservation may be extended by a further 180-day period upon application made before expiry, per the Companies Regulations 2011.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole model for this licensed industry. The Companies Act 71 of 2008 section 23 requires every company to maintain a registered office at a physical South African address accessible for service of process. Critically, the South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA), implementing the Maritime Labour Convention 2006 and the STCW Convention, requires a licensed seafarer recruitment and placement service to sustain an operational physical premises with responsible personnel, employment records, and complaint-handling infrastructure. A virtual mailbox may supplement, but cannot replace, the physical registered office and operational base.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — approximately 65–75% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first licensing year by SAMSA or the Department of Employment and Labour, with additional periodic verification visits by CIPC for registered-office compliance and by the Financial Intelligence Centre for AML records on a risk-tier basis.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, sections 13, 14, 15, 19, 66 and 69; Companies Regulations 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: CoR 15.1 Notice of Incorporation and Memorandum of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a private company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; the MOI may fix a nominal share capital, and the subscriber's escrowed subscription funds can be applied on incorporation. No escrow account is mandated by CIPC unless funds are held pending conditions in an MOI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the subscribers of ZA_PTY_LTD, that: (1) the subscribers be and are hereby allotted 100 ordinary shares as set out in the Memorandum of Incorporation, and the agreed subscription consideration, being no less than the nominal value, be credited as paid-up capital; (2) the registered office address described in the Notice of Incorporation is adopted, and the Company's statutory records shall be kept there; (3) the persons named in the subscription documents are appointed as directors, with the presiding director and financial officer appointed to execute banking, employment, and regulatory engagements; (4) the directors are authorized to procure maritime crew recruitment licences and to make all statutory filings. Adopted unanimously and recorded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services Platform / Companies and Intellectual Property Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search, then file CoR 9.1 for reservation of up to three preferred names. Payment is made online via CIPC using card or electronic funds transfer. Notarization is not required; digital identity is verified by CIPC.
required_dossiers: Completed CIPC CoR 9.1 name reservation form
Identity or passport copies of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit alternative names or file a formal appeal to CIPC with supporting explanation within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI using the CIPC standard template or custom provisions; all incorporators and initial directors must sign the MOI; execute CoR 15.1 with prescribed particulars and consent forms.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 consent to act as director
Verified identity documents of incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC will notify of material defects; correct and resubmit the documents through e-Services with re-attached signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing, Fee Payment and Incorporation Lodgement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed corporate documents, effect the prescribed fee payment, and submit the incorporation pack. CIPC will verify compliance with Companies Act sections 13 and 14 and issue the final registration number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pay the resubmission fee and cure identified statutory non-compliances within the CIPC notice period, typically 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Registration Certificate and Company File Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, CIPC issues a Registration Certificate containing the company registration number, registration date and legal name. Open the statutory registers at the registered office and record directors and shareholders.
required_dossiers: MOI and notice of incorporation copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of certificate particulars by written application to CIPC supported by the MOI and a registered office confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS and Compensation Fund Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and Compensation Fund (COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, PAYE, UIF and SDL via SARS eFiling; register with the Compensation Fund for employee injury and occupational disease coverage; obtain a Tax Compliance Status certificate for public-sector and corporate engagements.
required_dossiers: SARS and Compensation Fund registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct mismatched names or registration numbers on eFiling; submit manual registration applications to the relevant SARS branch or Compensation Fund office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Commercial Bank Account and Appoint Authorised Persons
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank in South Africa (e.g., Standard Bank, FNB, Absa, Nedbank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the board resolution and certified corporate documents to the selected bank; complete FICA identity and source-of-funds verification for all signatories and beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Signed board resolution authorizing bank account opening
Directors' identity and proof of residential address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide bank-specific governance documents, corrected resolutions, or further beneficial-ownership information to satisfy the bank's account opening committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (Employment Services Branch) and South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Agency Registration (Maritime Sector) / Ship Crew Recruitment and Manning Agency Licence

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Basic Registration — office-based maritime crew agency does not trigger a full Environmental Impact Assessment under the EIA Regulations Listing Notices unless physical crew training or industrial manning infrastructure is established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent; office-generated wastewater is discharged to municipal sewer in compliance with the National Water Act 36 of 1998. All waste storage and handling must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, and VOC emission thresholds are not triggered for this administrative service activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance with SANS 10400 Part T fire protection and a municipal fire clearance certificate for the registered office; Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 section 8 risk assessment and section 19 workplace inspection; no significant structural load clearance required beyond the building certificate of occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply for income tax registration via SARS eFiling, appointing a SARS-registered tax representative. A (Pty) Ltd is automatically registered for corporate income tax upon incorporation through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) and SARS integration. Income tax reference numbers are issued electronically; VAT registration (SARS 101 or 102 form) is required separately upon meeting threshold or carrying on enterprise activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - Proprietary Limited Company (Pty) Ltd is taxed as a standalone legal entity under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, subject to corporate income tax at the prevailing rate (27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023), with no pass-through attributes. The company is a resident tax entity if incorporated in South Africa or if its place of effective management is in South Africa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box classification system. Available statutory elections include: voluntary VAT registration (where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 under Section 23 of the VAT Act), VAT grouping election under Section 50A of the VAT Act, and rollover relief elections for corporate restructuring under Sections 42-45 of the Income Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory pursuant to Sections 8G and 8H of the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration is required when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 (One Million Rand) in any rolling 12-month period. Voluntary registration is permitted when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in the preceding 12 months.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS has not mandated universal real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping for all VAT vendors. Vendors must issue standard tax invoices containing prescribed particulars under Section 20(4) of the VAT Act. All VAT returns (VAT201) and supporting schedules must be submitted electronically via SARS eFiling. SARS employs automated risk engines and data analytics to audit VAT claims, including export zero-rating substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies to goods exported from South Africa under Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, provided the vendor retains proof of export within the mandated period. Crew management and recruitment services supplied to non-resident ship owners, or for vessels engaged in international seagoing trade, qualify for zero-rating under Section 11(2)(k) (services supplied to non-residents) or Section 11(2)(l) (services physically rendered outside South Africa). The service recipient must be a non-resident and the services must not be used or consumed in South Africa. Specific documentation must evidence the non-resident supply and flow of consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500) or electronic pre-entry
Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill for airfreight)
Inward Remittance Certificate or Form A exchange control approval evidencing receipt of consideration
Signed contract or engagement letter evidencing the non-resident recipient and place of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS High Risk Investigation Units and Customs Audit Units rigorously verify export zero-rating claims. Deficiencies in proof of export lead to refund clawbacks, disallowance of the zero-rating, and additional VAT assessed at 15%. The Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 imposes substantial understatement penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall for gross negligence or intentional disregard of the law. Section 60 of the VAT Act prescribes criminal penalties, including fines and imprisonment, for fraudulent zero-rating and evasion. Records must be retained for a minimum of five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB); Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) administers exchange control under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, acting through Authorised Dealers which are domestic banks with foreign exchange dealing licences.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is a managed-convertible currency rather than a fully free-floating currency without controls. Current account transactions, including trade in services, crew recruitment fees, and ordinary operational repatriations, are largely liberalised and may proceed through Authorised Dealers without prior SARB approval, subject to documentary verification. Capital account flows, including inward equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, and outward direct investment, remain subject to exchange-control authorisation and reporting. Dividends and branch profits of a solvent (Pty) Ltd are remittable to non-resident shareholders after compliance with the Companies Act solvency and liquidity test and after deduction of South African dividends tax, which is currently 20%, subject to applicable tax treaty reduction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: It is mandatory for services exports, including ship crew recruitment and crewing-management services, to be paid and repatriated to South Africa within 180 days from the date the service is performed or the invoice becomes due, whichever event occurs first. Export proceeds received in foreign currency must be surrendered to an Authorised Dealer in exchange for rand, unless FinSurv has granted a Foreign Currency Account dispensation permitting retention within prescribed limits. The surrender obligation applies at 100% of the repatriated foreign currency proceeds, and any deviation requires a prior FinSurv approval or an explicit Authorised Dealer-documented exemption for approved imports, debt servicing, or foreign tax payments.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (ZAR and multi-currency) for fee collections and payroll disbursements; Capital Escrow Account for inward non-resident capital injection

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: First National Bank, a division of FirstRand Bank Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with integrated FX desk and payroll API; Capital Escrow Account for share capital holding and compliance monitoring
Operational Account and International Banking Account; Capital Escrow Account for exchange-control controlled inward funds
Operational Account with cross-border payroll streaming; Capital Escrow Account for structured inbound treasury transactions
Multi-currency Current Account and Treasury Settlement Account for high-value cross-border flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium, conditional. Offshore fintech EMIs and virtual account providers are not licensed as banks or Authorised Dealers under the Banks Act 90 of 1990 and cannot independently hold ZAR accounts or perform SARB exchange-control functions. They may support low-value payroll disbursement execution through a licensed partner bank, but all inward capital, export-proceeds conversion, and South African regulatory reporting obligations must be discharged through a domestic Authorised Dealer. Legal viability therefore requires a local approved account as the primary treasury spine, with offshore EMI rails used only as supplementary disbursement channels and never as the sole clearing and settlement venue.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for a physical interview in every instance, but FICA mandates that the bank identify and verify each director, each beneficial owner holding 10% or more of the company, and each natural-person signatory using reliable and independent documentation. In practice, Tier-1 South African banks require at least one director with board authority to attend an in-person or notarised verification appointment; remote opening is possible only where the bank has a functional e-KYC platform, the director’s passport is notarised, a biometric verification is completed, and the board resolution granting account authority is original. Foreign directors without a South African physical presence should expect certified true copies of passports, proof of residential address, a reference from an existing foreign banking relationship, and a video interview with the bank’s AML team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership obscurity, including offshore trusts, interposed holding companies, or nominee shareholders above the 10% threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC issued share register, Memorandum of Incorporation, trust deed or Foundation deed, full organisational chart to ultimate natural persons, sworn proof of source of wealth, notarised passports of all natural persons, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the intermediate holding tier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payroll disbursements to seafarers in high-risk, sanctioned, or restricted jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid STCW certificates and seafarer employment agreements, crew matrix, payroll instruction files with bank and SWIFT details, sanctions screening logs, proof of visa and work-authorisation status, certificates of ownership of the vessel, and evidence of the underlying crewing order from the vessel operator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party mandates where shipowners or ship managers make payments into a designated crewing agency collection account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed crewing agreement, mandate letter from the third party, board resolution accepting the third-party arrangement, flow-of-funds chart, debtor acknowledgement, and KYC/KYB documentation on the third-party payee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or dealings with vessels under OFAC, UN, EU, or UK sanctions flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel screening using IMO/ISIS and commercial sanctions databases, end-use and end-user declarations, OFAC/UN/EU/UK sanctions-screening evidence, shipmaster certificate, flag registration certificate, and shipowner UBO declaration, all retained for audit and ready for submission to the Authorised Dealer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual invoicing patterns, including absence of VAT output invoices or misaligned commission calculations on crew payroll
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SARS VAT registration certificate, tax clearance status, fully itemised commercial invoices, payroll computation schedules, crewing-fee calculation notes, bank reconciliation statements, and signed board-approved fee-schedule evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concerns for the initial capital contribution by a non-resident shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder’s bank statements for at least 12 months, share subscription agreement, proof of lawful origin of funds, tax clearance from the home jurisdiction, board resolution approving the capital injection, and share certificates issued after payment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inward capital injections must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder’s bank account to the South African (Pty) Ltd’s account at an Authorised Dealer, with full compliance with the specified balance-of-payments purpose code for inward direct investment or shareholder loan. The wire message must identify the South African beneficiary company, the non-resident remitter, the transaction reference, and the purpose narrative e.g. ‘inward equity subscription’ or ‘shareholder loan’ as determined by the Authorised Dealer’s exchange-control system. Supporting verification comprises the CIPC registration certificate, Memorandum of Incorporation, board resolution, share subscription or loan agreement, and a formal declaration of the non-resident status of the shareholder. The Authorised Dealer will record the inflow for FinSurv reporting and will monitor subsequent repatriation or disinvestment for capital-control compliance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for crew recruitment operations, seafarer payroll, and vessel management services will be cleared primarily through: (a) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for foreign-currency payments to seafarer bank accounts, recruitment subcontractors, and offshore payees; (b) commercial documentary letters of credit for settlement of high-value vessel supplies, equipment purchases, and crew-change logistics; (c) SAMOS, the South African Multiple Option Settlement system, for domestic ZAR payroll, tax payments, and local supplier settlements; and (d) regional African clearing corridors via correspondent banks for US-dollar, euro, and rand settlements inside the SADC and SACU markets. All outbound foreign payments are subject to the Authorised Dealer’s exchange-control review, with invoice and contract evidence required for each disbursement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (DFs) for hedging ZAR/USD, ZAR/EUR, and ZAR/GBP operational exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-deliverable emerging-market currencies in the crew recruitment corridor, provided there is a verified underlying commercial exposure
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for matching foreign-currency denominated shareholder loans and larger vessel-owner contracts
FX swaps and forward roll-overs for treasury liquidity matching and settlement-date risk
Specialist FX options, including only cost-of-carry structures and hedged option strategies, where the bank confirms an underlying trade or payroll exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) for Proprietary Limited Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 business days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty ZAR 180 in the first year and ZAR 580 per subsequent year; default beyond 40 business days triggers a CIPC compliance notice; two consecutive years of default may lead to deregistration under s.82, Companies Act 71 of 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) Annual Confirmation and Change-of-Control Notice (Form BE2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (integrated with the Annual Return filing channel)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation with the Annual Return; any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding control must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Wilful non-compliance is a criminal offence (fine and/or imprisonment up to 10 years); CIPC may reject the Annual Return and withhold good-standing certificates; directors bear statutory liability for false or omitted beneficial ownership particulars.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) and Supporting Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 12 months after the financial year-end (dates confirmed by SARS annual public notice); provisional tax returns (IRP6) due 6 months after commencement and on the last day of the year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011: late-payment penalty of 10% plus 10% per completed month on unpaid tax; understatement penalty of 10%-150% depending on conduct; administrative non-compliance penalties for non-filing may reach ZAR 16,000 per month.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Small Business Corporations (SBCs) with gross income below ZAR 20 million are taxed at progressive rates of 0%-21%. Ordinary deductions under section 11(a) apply to crew recruitment operating costs, payroll, and licensed crewing expenses. Renewable energy allowances under section 12B and learnership allowances under section 12H are available where eligible. The crew agency does not automatically qualify for special economic zone or industrial tax incentives unless physically located in a designated SEZ.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 Company Income Tax Return submitted via SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, supplemented by semi-annual provisional tax returns (IRP6) and six-monthly provisional tax payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the financial year-end, as specified by the SARS notice of assessment. Provisional tax estimates are payable at the end of the first half-year and at year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS taxpayer reference number and company registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must provide their foreign tax identification number and, where applicable, a South African taxpayer reference obtained through SARS registration as a non-resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial year-end date and reporting currency
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The return must be completed in ZAR; foreign-currency transactions are translated using the spot rate or the average rate acceptable to SARS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from crew recruitment, vessel management, payroll facilitation, and other revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income sourced in South Africa, including agency fees for placing seafarers with South African shipowners or vessels operating from South African ports, must be declared. Income sourced outside South Africa is included only where the controlled foreign company rules or residence basis apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions, including crewing salaries, marine insurance, port fees, communications, office rent, and professional licences
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowable only to the extent incurred in the production of South African-sourced income and supported by contemporaneous records. Payments to non-resident subcontractors are subject to transfer pricing and withholding rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting assessed losses and section 18A donations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An assessed loss may be carried forward for the statutory period only if the company maintains continuity of trade. Non-resident owners cannot offset foreign losses against South African taxable income unless the loss arises from South African trade.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Normal tax computation at 27%, reduced by provisional tax payments rebated
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies are taxed on South African-source income at the same 27% rate. Dividend, interest, and royalty withholding taxes are separate final taxes and are not deducted in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all South African withholding taxes. The non-resident beneficial owner may claim treaty relief only where the prescribed DTA declaration and tax residence certificate are provided to the withholding agent before payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: SARS imposes a percentage-based non-compliance penalty of up to 200% of the tax liability understatement, an administrative monthly penalty of up to ZAR 250 per day for a maximum of 12 months, interest on outstanding tax at the statutory rate (prime plus 3%), and possible criminal prosecution for fraudulent returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final dividends tax, applied to the gross dividend declared to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a tax residence certificate from its home tax authority, complete the SARS DTA declaration, and deliver both to the South African dividend-withholding agent before the dividend payment date. The reduced treaty rate is applied at source only after the declaration is accepted by the company, transfer secretary, or bank.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory rate, reduced to 0%-10% under many DTA treaties. Interest: 15% statutory rate, with numerous treaties reducing the rate to 0%-10%. Both are final withholding taxes in respect of payments to non-resident beneficial owners.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required where aggregate affected cross-border related-party transactions exceed ZAR 5 million in the year of assessment; Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds ZAR 10 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not operate a dedicated Economic Substance Regulations registry. Instead, SARS applies the place of effective management residence test, controlled foreign company attribution rules, general anti-avoidance provisions, earnings stripping limits on interest deductions, and transfer pricing recharacterisation. A crew recruitment agency must maintain a real local office, employment contracts, decision-making records, operational bank accounts, and substantive maritime staffing activity; a paper shell without local management is vulnerable to recharacterisation and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting crew placement fees, maintaining off-book payroll, inflating crew wages or marine expenses, issuing false invoices, and failing to declare South African-source income from seafarer supply contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty of 150% of the resulting tax shortfall, interest, criminal fine equal to the evaded tax, and imprisonment for up to five years under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate in or direct the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax under section 160. Civil recovery, asset attachment, departure restrictions, and imprisonment apply; the corporate veil is pierced on proof of reckless or fraudulent trading.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Obtaining or maintaining a crew recruitment licence without any physical office, employed maritime staffing managers, bank account, or genuine commercial activity; routing payments through a South African entity solely to access SACU maritime or port-market benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS can recharacterise the arrangement under the general anti-avoidance rules, disregard the shell entity, impose a 100% penalty, and cancel the crew recruitment licence. The Companies and Intellectual Property Commission may deregister the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for all debts and tax liabilities if the company is found to be recklessly or fraudulently trading under Companies Act sections 77 and 218. Directors face disqualification, civil restitution, and travel bans pending tax collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Intelligence Centre Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register as an accountable institution, failing to conduct client due diligence on shipowners and seafarers, processing anonymous cash payroll, or using undisclosed foreign bank accounts to launder proceeds from illegal vessel crew trafficking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to ZAR 10 million under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, criminal fines, and imprisonment up to 15 years for money laundering under POCA. The licence may be revoked and the business closed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly allow money laundering face criminal liability, asset forfeiture, civil damages, travel restrictions, and imprisonment. SARS may also seek personal collection from directors under the Tax Administration Act where the non-compliance facilitated tax evasion.
